question.leadin: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war.
question.text: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
question.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

swap.leadin: This leader was nicknamed the "Iron Chancellor" for conducting diplomacy using the strategy of Realpolitik.
swap.text: Name this Prussian statesman, who masterminded the Unification of Germany.
swap.clue: This man edited the Ems Dispatch to provoke the Franco-Prussian War.

question.leadin: Name these things associated with the unification of Germany.
question.text: Germany had been unified after various German lands had come together to defeat France in this war in 1870.
question.clue: Its immediate cause was the candidacy of Leopold for the Spanish throne, though some of the pretext was provided by an imagined insult to Count Benedetti.

swap.leadin: During a failed coup d'etat, this man attempted to put Erich Ludendorff in power.
swap.text: For 10 points, name this man, who, after his arrest for his leadership in that Beer Hall Putsch, composed Mein Kampf from his prison cell.
swap.clue: Hans Ritter von Seisser and Otto von Lossow put down a rebellion led by this leader, and he consolidated power by executing Operation Hummingbird.

question.text: This West German Social Democrat chancellor sought to improve ties with the Soviet bloc. He resigned as chancellor after his advisor Gunter Guillaume was discovered to be a member of the East German secret police.
question.clue: Known as the "Chancellor of Domestic Reform," this man spent 16 years as president of the Socialist International after leaving his highest position due to the Guillaume affair, which revealed his aide to be a Stasi agent.

swap.text: This northernmost state borders Denmark to the north and has its capital at Kiel.
swap.clue: John Russell attempted to solve a dispute involving this region by convening the London Conference of 1864, whose annexation violated the earlier London Protocol of 1852.

question.text: Christina presided over the middle of Sweden's time as a Great Power, which began, roughly, with the decline of this organization. This organization of Baltic cities was dominated by Lubeck in the Middle Ages.
question.clue: It gained power after a treaty giving them access to the Russian port of Novgorod from its base city of Lubeck, but trade there was banned by Ivan III.

swap.leadin: Name some responses to World War I.
swap.text: The War Guilt Clause contributed to the destabilization of this interwar German government, named for the city where its constitution was drafted.
swap.clue: The Spartacist League disbanded shortly after this government executed its leaders Walter Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg.

question.leadin: Name these other Nazis who died in grisly fashion.
question.text: Just two hours before he was to be executed, this founder of the Gestapo and air minister poisoned himself.
question.clue: Near the end of the war, this man sent a telegram to Hitler in which he announced he would take control of the Reich, prompting Hitler to angrily change his will.

swap.leadin: A 1919 uprising led by this organization was crushed by Freikorps supporting the Centrist policies of Friedrich Ebert.
swap.text: Identify this Marxist organization which briefly became the Communist Party of Germany, founded by Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg and named for an earlier revolutionary.
swap.clue: This organization was the first to publish the Red Flag newspaper, and its prominent members included August Thalheimer and Clara Zetkin.

question.text: The war was ended by this treaty, which also recognized Prussia's conquest of Silesia.
question.clue: Madras was transferred to the British after a short French rule as a provision of this Treaty, whose other terms included the transfer of some Italian duchies to Spain. It essentially reverted to the terms established by the Treaty of Utrecht

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a former Soviet satellite state.
swap.text: This quantum chemist is, to date, the only person raised in the GDR ever to have been German Chancellor, an office which they held for 16 years.
swap.clue: This leader unsuccessfully sought a Jamaica coalition after the SPD initially declined to continue its grand coalition with the Christian Democratic Union.

question.text: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
question.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen [or Manfred Albrecht Freiherr von Richthofen; or the Red Baron]
question.clue: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.

swap.text: The Germans achieved success near the end of the War by using these troops to break the trench stalemate. Oskar von Hutier pioneered their tactics, which were used to great success during the Ludendorff Offensive.
swap.answerHtml: stormtroopers [or stoßtruppen; sturmmann; sturmtruppen; prompt on translations like shock troops or assault troops]
swap.clue: German victory at Caporetto was partially due to the use of these soldiers. These units used "infiltration tactics" to overwhelm enemy trenches, and their name in German roughly translates as "shock troops."

question.text: The secular electors included the margrave of this northeastern German state, which merged into Prussia in the 1600s.
question.clue: A later (emphasize) elector of this state invited expelled French Huguenots to settle after the Edict of Fontainebleau and, thanks to his military successes in neighboring Pomerania, was called the "Great Elector".

swap.text: A royal opponent of the 1832 Reform Bill was this uncle of Queen Victoria who served as Duke of Clarence and became the first person since George I to be the ruler of Hanover but not the ruler of Britain.
swap.answerHtml: Ernest Augustus I of Hanover [or Duke of Clarence before mention; prompt on “Ernest Augustus”]

question.text: Luther also opposed this group of Anabaptists influenced by Thomas Muntzer. This group, which included Thomas Dreschal and Nicholas Storch, believed themselves to receive messages directly from God.
question.clue: This collective name for three religious agitators whose names were probably Nicholas Storch, Thomas Dreschel, and Marcus Stubner.

swap.leadin: Sheila Ogilvie's State Corporatism and Proto-Industry argues that this German state's legacy of rent-seeking by worsted-weaving guilds delayed mechanization until after 1870.
swap.text: Name this Swabian state where Wilhelm Maybach designed engines at Daimler Motors after the Peace of Pressburg made it and Bavaria into kingdoms. In 1952, it united with the home state of Carl Benz.
swap.answerHtml: Württemberg (“WUR-tem-bairk”) [accept Baden-Württemberg or BW or BaWü; accept Kingdom of Württemberg or Königreich Württemberg; accept Duchy of Württemberg or Herzogtum Württemberg; accept Free People’s State of Württemberg or Freier Volksstaat Württemberg; reject “Baden”]

question.text: While the attempts to collapse the British economy were unsuccessful, the counterfeit money was allegedly used to pay this man for his work rescuing Benito Mussolini in the Gran Sasso raid. During Operation Panzerfaust, this man kidnapped Miklos Horthy's ("MEEK-lohsh HOR-tee's") son and forced Horthy to resign.
question.clue: This man planned the kidnapping of Miklos Horthy's son in Operation Panzerfaust, as well as Operation Greif, in which his men pretended to be Allied troops during the Battle of the Bulge.

swap.text: The Austrians were joined at Koniggratz by soldiers from this kingdom. Frederick the Wise was an elector of this place.
swap.clue: During World War I, George V renamed a royal house named for this region, Coburg, and Gotha to the House of Windsor.
